target_customer: Personal injury law firms (mostly plaintiffs' firms) that pay for client communication software
problem: Injury clients feel uninformed about their case and firms spend staff time on status calls and texts. Hona pulls milestones from the firm's case management system and sends client updates automatically.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription sold to law firms, integrated with case management systems
product_category: Legal tech, client communication and engagement automation

founders.name: Josh Christensen
previous_startups: J-Slips Hawaii (e-commerce sandals, scaled past $1M revenue in two years per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Taught himself to code. Source: YC company page.

founders.name: Matt McClellan
founders.background_notes: YC page and LawNext give no background. Company site lists him as CEO.

founders.name: Manny Griffiths
founders.background_notes: LawNext (July 2023) names him cofounder and CEO and says the idea came from his wife's experience after a 2018 car accident. He is not on the YC page or the current company site, so his later role is unknown.

technical_complexity.rationale: In 2021 to 2023 the core product was integrations with a dozen plus case management systems plus text and email triggers. This is integration work more than research. AI agent features came later (Lia launch covered by ABA Journal).

defensibility.rationale: Integrations with Filevine, Clio, CASEpeer, MyCase and others and compliance work take time to replicate, but the case management vendors could add similar features themselves.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Case management vendors already bundled client portals and texting, but as of the sources found they partnered with Hona through integrations (CASEpeer partnership announced March 2023) rather than buying it. No acquisition found.

market_need_then: LawNext (July 2023) reports the founder's wife felt her lawyer never kept her informed. The company had over $1M ARR and over 20 employees by July 2023, which shows firms were paying for client updates.

branding.name_origin: Renamed from Milestones in July 2023. LawNext says the team picked Hona because everyone liked it and it is intentionally vague about what the company does so it would not limit growth. No meaning for the word is stated.
branding.domain_note: Moved from getmilestones.com to hona.com at the July 2023 rebrand, per the company's rebrand announcement reported by SmartBranding.

identity.mascot_or_character: Lia, the AI agent (product persona, not a mascot)
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, reassuring, focused on clarity and transparency for clients

branding.brand_signature: Early pitch line: the Domino's Pizza Tracker for legal services

rebrands.why: Milestones no longer fit once the product added two-way messaging, documents and non-linear case types; shorter domain also cited

brand_strength.rationale: The name is short and ownable but vague. Sources show press on the rebrand but no evidence of community, merch or word of mouth driven by the brand itself.

pivots.from: One-way milestone notifications for clients of service businesses (Milestones)
pivots.to: Two-way client messaging, documents and later an AI agent for personal injury firms (Hona)
pivots.why: Expanded into practice areas where case progress is not linear

outcome_analysis: Hona grew from the Milestones notification tool into a client communication platform with over $1M ARR by mid 2023, a $2.1M seed in July 2023 and a $9.5M Series A in June 2024. Its site now claims 500+ personal injury firms. Integrations with the major case management systems and a clear pain point drove growth. The company is active with 32 people per the YC page, and no layoffs, sale or shutdown were found.
notes: Founder lists conflict: the YC page names Josh Christensen and Matt McClellan, LawNext 2023 names Manny Griffiths and Matt McClellan, the company site names McClellan (CEO) and Christensen (CTO). LawNext says the company was based in Lehi, Utah while YC lists Orem. LawNext says it had earlier raised $500K pre-seed and finished YC in March 2023; this is probably the YC deal and is not recorded as a round. Dealroom's 2024 valuation range of 50 to 100M is paywalled and not recorded. A competitor search with date terms found only 2023 integration partner announcements, no dated competitor, so the list is empty.
